To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MF-synthesized polymer-lipid hybrid nanoparticle loaded siRNA is a promising therapeutic for intractable disease.

MF-synthesized polymer-lipid hybrid NPs (P/LNPS) loaded with VEGFR1 siRNA demonstrated low vehicle cytotoxcity, potent tumor cell inhibition both in vitro and prolonged blood circulation in vivo, and greater down-regulation in tumor VEGF mRNA/protein levels as well as tumor inhibition in vivo compared to BM-synthesized P/NPs.
MF synthesis of P/LNPs is an efficient method for preparing siRNA therapeutics for in vitro and in-vivo applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel microfluidic hydrodynamically focused synthesis method for the production of P/LNPs.
the development of microfluidic hydrodynamics focusing technology to prepare polymer-lipid hybrid siRNA nanoparticles for cancer therapy.
the development of a microfluidic chip for preparation of polymer-lipids hybrid nanoparticles for delivery of small interfering RNAs ( siRNAs) as a potential therapy for cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MF system is a promising approach for the preparation of P/LNPs for siRNA delivery in vivo.
MF-synthesized PLNPs are a promising siRNA delivery system that can be further evaluated in preclinical models of cancer.
MF synthesis of P/LNPs is a simple, efficient, and reproducible approach for siRNA delivery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MF-synthesized polymer-lipid hybrid NPs can be used for siRNA delivery to inhibit tumor growth.
MF-synthesized polymer-lipid hybrid NPs are an efficient and safe siRNA delivery system with potential for cancer therapy.
MF-synthesized PLNP is a promising therapeutic delivery platform for siRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microfluidic hydrodynamically focused synthesis of polymer-ligand hybrid nanoparticles can be used to produce a safe and effective siRNA delivery system.
MF is a promising method for producing polymer-lipid hybrid NPs that are effective and safe for therapeutic delivery of small interfering RNA.
MF can be used to prepare polymer-lipid hybrid nanoparticle (P/LN) for siRNA delivery and the P/LNPs can be used to treat cancer.
